fixes.title: Pre-flight dark-library check uses the camera default temperature (-10C), not the temperature the sequence's Cool Camera node will actually reach (15C)
fixes.summary: Closed in the working tree by an earlier wave, at the location the verifier corrected the finding to. packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/preflight_rules.dart:122 builds plannedTemps via _plannedSensorTemps (:256-277), which walks the tree in execution order threading the setpoint: a CoolCameraNode changes it for everything that follows, and the camera's live setpoint is only used until the first one. Line 138-140 stamps each DarkFrameRequirement with the setpoint that node will execute at, so the 'Capture missing darks' action can no longer offer to capture at a temperature the run never uses. Nothing about it is disclosure-only: the matched temperature itself changed (the extra 'Temperatures are the setpoints this sequence cools to' line at :195-197 is added ON TOP).
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/sequence/preflight_rules_test.dart - 'DarkLibraryCoverageRule uses the setpoint the sequence cools to, not the live one' and 'clean when the library holds darks at the cooled setpoint'
fixes.revert_check: Replaced preflight_rules.dart:138-140 `final plannedTemp = plannedTemps.containsKey(node.id) ? plannedTemps[node.id] : camTargetTemp;` with `final plannedTemp = camTargetTemp;` -> 2 tests fail (+2 -2). Restored -> 42 pass.

fixes.title: Captured frames are written to the DB with NO gain, offset, sensor temperature, mount pointing, focuser position or target link
fixes.summary: Closed in the working tree. The capture truth the FITS writer used travels on the frame event as FrameCaptureMetadata (native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/event.rs:981) and is read once at packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/sequence_executor/event_operations.dart:638; the insertSequenceFrame call at :765-821 now passes sensorTemp/coolerPower/mountRa/mountDec/mountAltitude/mountAzimuth/pierSide/focuserPosition/focuserTemp/rotatorAngle plus gain/offset/binning/frameType/exposure taken from what the camera reported rather than from the node config. target_id is bound at run start (see the 'Untargeted' entry).
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/sequence/sequence_frame_capture_metadata_test.dart - 'accepted frame persists every capture field the FITS header carries' + 'rejected frame persists the same capture fields'
fixes.revert_check: Changed event_operations.dart:800 `sensorTemp: capture.sensorTempC,` to `sensorTemp: null,` -> both tests fail. Restored -> all 15 pass.

fixes.title: Four surfaces disagree about which filter a frame was taken through: filename says 'nofilter', DB says 'R', FITS header has no FILTER card, run stats say 'Unknown'
fixes.summary: The previous wave made each SIDE internally consistent but left the two sides independently derived, so they still diverged. Rust resolves the burst's (name, slot) once (instructions.rs resolve_burst_filter/resolve_frame_filter) and stamps it into the filename and the FITS FILTER/FILTPOS cards. Dart resolved its own answer for captured_images.filter and the stats bucket from sequenceProgressProvider.currentFilter ?? filterWheelStateProvider - and currentFilter is only ever written by a ChangeFilter node's ProgressDetail::Filter or by SequencerEvent.ExposureStarted.filter, which carries the NODE's static config.filter (executor/mod.rs:2690-2704). So a burst that addresses the wheel by slot only (filter_index set, filter null) after an earlier Change Filter to L wrote FILTER='R' and _R_ into the file while the database row said 'L'. Fixed at the source: ExposeInstruction now publishes the pair it resolved (node/instructions/expose.rs:82-95) through the existing ProgressDetail::Filter channel, so the DB column and the stats bucket read the same value the header was written from. Verified the publish cannot be undone downstream: SequenceProgressNotifier.updateProgress treats a null currentFilter as 'no change' (sequence_progress.dart:79), so the per-frame ExposureStarted with a null filter that follows does not wipe it.
fixes.test: Rust: instructions.rs::tests::burst_publishes_the_filter_identity_it_resolved (wheel parked on slot 1 'R', earlier Change Filter left 'L', node addresses slot 1 by index) asserts the FITS filter_name is R AND that exactly one ProgressDetail::Filter{name:'R',position:1} was published. Dart: sequence_executor_run_record_truth_test.dart 'a Take Exposures burst that resolved the wheel itself wins over a stale Change Filter' drives the exact published payload (instruction 'Exposure', detail_kind 'Filter') plus a null-filter ExposureStarted and asserts the run-stats bucket is 'R'.
fixes.revert_check: Deleted the emission block at expose.rs:82-95 -> `burst_publishes_the_filter_identity_it_resolved` fails with left: [] right: [("R", Some(1))]. Restored -> 729 sequencer tests pass, cargo fmt --check clean.

fixes.title: Frames captured under a named target are reported as 'Untargeted', and the run's target breakdown is keyed by the SEQUENCE name instead of the target name
fixes.summary: Closed in the working tree by two production changes, both revert-verified. (a) captured_images.target_id: SequenceExecutor._bindCatalogTargets (sequence_executor.dart:636-663) gives every named Target node a `targets` row at run start and _runTargetIdFor (:667-671) stamps it on each frame, so session_report_service.dart:207-209 resolves the real name instead of its 'Untargeted' bucket. (b) the stats bucket key: _resolveActiveTargetName (event_operations.dart:940-955) falls back to the enclosing TargetHeaderNode before the sequence name, so targetBreakdown is keyed 'New Target', not 'New Sequence'.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/sequence/sequence_executor_run_lifecycle_test.dart group 'M. frames are attributed to the target that produced them'; packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/sequence/run_record_error_and_target_test.dart group 'run stats are bucketed by the target, not the sequence'
fixes.revert_check: (a) sequence_executor.dart:670 `return header.catalogTargetId ?? _runCatalogTargetIds[header.id];` -> `return header.catalogTargetId;` fails 'a builder-authored target gets a catalog row and the frame points at it'. (b) deleting the enclosingTargetHeader fallback at event_operations.dart:945-951 fails 'a frame under a Target node is filed under that target'. Both restored, both suites green.

fixes.title: A single failing Dither node is reported as two identical errors, in the report and in two stacked critical banners
fixes.summary: Both halves are closed, and they are two different code paths - the previous wave's note only covered one. (1) The run record: the bridge emits a mid-run SequencerEvent::Error for InstructionFailed and the executor re-formats the SAME failure into the terminal SequenceFailed reason; event_operations.dart:986 now routes terminal reasons through SequenceRunStats.recordTerminalError (sequence_stats_provider.dart:176), which drops a message identical to the immediately-preceding one while mid-run recordError still records genuine repeats. (2) The on-screen banner/toast, which the verifier could not check: it does NOT read the run's error list, it reads runDashboardCriticalEventsProvider off the event stream, so the stats de-dup could not have fixed it. That path has its own guard, _isRestatedFailureReason (run_dashboard_providers.dart:765-783, called at :845), which remembers each escalated mid-run reason for the current run and skips the terminal restatement of it.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/sequence/terminal_error_not_recorded_twice_test.dart (3 tests); packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/widgets/run_dashboard/terminal_failure_not_double_escalated_test.dart (4 tests, covers the banner/toast half)
fixes.revert_check: Changed event_operations.dart:986 `stats.recordTerminalError(message)` to `stats.recordError(message)` -> 'one failed node produces one error entry, not two' fails. Restored -> 3 pass. The banner suite passes as-is (4/4).

fixes.title: sequence_runs.status stays 'running' while the run is paused, so any non-GUI consumer thinks the rig is still exposing
fixes.summary: Closed in the working tree. SequenceExecutor.pause() writes 'paused' and resume() writes 'running' back (sequence_executor.dart:1333 / :1370 via _persistLiveRunStatus at :1382 -> SequenceRunsDao.setLiveStatus, sequence_runs_dao.dart:98), and the startup crash-recovery sweep was widened to `status IN ('running','paused')` (migration_strategy.dart:57) so a process that dies mid-pause cannot leave a permanently stale live row. I checked the inversion risk the campaign warns about: nothing else in the app selects rows by status == 'running', so nothing loses sight of the active run while it is paused. The consumer the finding names is real - apps/desktop/lib/headless_api/handlers/db_read_handlers.dart:142 and :698 serve `row.status` verbatim to the web dashboard and the phone.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/sequence/sequence_executor_run_lifecycle_test.dart group 'L. the run row publishes pause' - 'pausing writes paused, resuming writes running back' + 'a row left paused by a dead process is closed out on open'
fixes.revert_check: Deleted `await _persistLiveRunStatus('paused');` at sequence_executor.dart:1333 -> 'pausing writes paused, resuming writes running back' fails. Restored -> 43 pass.

fixes.title: The Continue Session handoff dialog says 'Unknown Profile' and 'No Sequence' while naming the sequence in its own header
fixes.summary: Closed at the upstream cause, not at the fallback string. The nulls were true: SessionStateNotifier.startSession was called without a profile or sequence id, so every imaging_sessions row had profile_id NULL / sequence_id NULL, and QuickStartService builds its context out of that row. SequenceExecutor._startSessionRow now passes them (sequence_executor.dart:607-608). Editing the 'Unknown Profile' literal in quick_start_dialog.dart would have been the disclosure-only non-fix.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/session_profile_sequence_binding_test.dart - 'the executor binds the run to its profile and sequence'
fixes.revert_check: Set sequence_executor.dart:607-608 to `profileId: null, sequenceId: null` -> the test fails. Restored -> 3 pass.

fixes.title: 'Load Previous Setup' is inert: it restores no equipment, no sequence and reports success anyway
fixes.summary: Closed on both halves the verifier separated. Behaviour: with the session row now carrying profile_id/sequence_id (previous entry), _handleStartFresh actually has something to restore - it activates the profile (quick_start_checker.dart:276-283), loads the sequence (:286-301) and applies the equipment snapshot (:304-309). Honesty: the primary button is disabled with an explicit reason when the session recorded none of the three (quick_start_dialog.dart:431 gate on _hasRestorableSetup, message at :448-450), and the snackbar is now worded from what was genuinely re-applied (:312-348) instead of the unconditional 'Loaded previous setup for previous target from frame 1' the verifier caught.

fixes.revert_check: Changed quick_start_dialog.dart:431 `else if (_hasRestorableSetup)` to `else if (true)` -> 'a session with nothing recorded cannot be loaded' fails. Restored -> 11 pass.

fixes.title: Builder and Pre-Flight disagree about how long the same sequence takes: '~18m 54s' vs 'Duration 27m'
fixes.summary: The previous wave collapsed three estimators into one (SequenceTimeEstimator) but left the pre-flight reading a different NUMBER off it, so the two surfaces still disagreed on any sequence that ends in a Count loop - which is most real sequences. estimateSequenceTiming deliberately emits detail for ONE pass of a Count loop (each entry carries a 'Showing 1 of N' note) while advancing its own clock by the whole loop; PreSessionSimulator took `segments.last.end` as the end of the run, so Pre-Flight's 'Duration' and 'Ends' billed a single iteration while the Builder chip, which reads estimateTotalDuration, billed all N. A Loop(count: 3) over a 2x120s body reads 4m 4s in Pre-Flight and 12m 12s in the Builder. pre_session_simulator.dart:114-124 now takes the later of the estimator's own walk end and the last rendered segment - the exact number the Builder chip shows - so the two cannot diverge; it can only move the end later, never earlier. Also repaired two skotiq_app tests that the previous wave's fix broke: wiring sequencerOverheadConfigProvider into sequenceTimelineProvider (visual_timeline.dart:43-49) made the timeline reach through SequencerDefaultsNotifier into the settings DAO, which throws MissingPluginException for path_provider under flutter_test.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/pre_session_simulator_test.dart - 'a sequence that ends in a Count loop is billed for every iteration, the same total the Builder estimate chip shows' asserts result.duration == estimator.estimateTotalDuration(...) == onePass * 3.
fixes.revert_check: Restored pre_session_simulator.dart:122-124 to `final end = segments.isEmpty ? start : segments.last.end;` -> the test fails with Expected 0:12:12 / Actual 0:04:04, exactly the loop factor. Restored -> 12 pass. Also confirmed the two skotiq_app timeline tests failed identically with my change stashed, i.e. they were broken by the previous wave, not by this one.
